title: Constant coefficients under a finite normalization comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be proper between finite-type $k$-schemes and
let $\nu:Y\to X$ be finite and surjective, in the conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose $\nu$ is an
isomorphism outside a reduced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$
for which $f|_Z$ is finite. Put $v=f\nu$, and let $M$ be a
finite module over the ring of [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions].
If all $R^qv_*\underline M$ are constructible, then so are all
$R^qf_*\underline M$. Moreover the natural map

$$
R^qf_*\underline M\longrightarrow R^qv_*\underline M
$$

is an isomorphism for every $q\geq2$.
Here constructibility and direct image have the meanings of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].
The notation $\underline M_T$ denotes the constant sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $T_{\Et}$. The natural comparison is induced by the adjunction unit $\underline M_X\to\nu_*\nu^{-1}\underline M_X$, identifying $\nu^{-1}\underline M_X$ with $\underline M_Y$, and the composition comparison for derived direct images; inverse image is as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Put $A=\underline M_X$, $B=\nu_*\underline M_Y$, and let $a:A\to B$ be the unit after the constant-sheaf pullback identification of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the stalk of a constant sheaf is $M$, with each constant section having germ the corresponding element of $M$. Under [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], $a_{\bar x}$ sends $m$ to $(m)_{\bar y}$: the unit restricts the constant section $m$ to the constant section $m$ on the inverse image of each neighbourhood. The finite fibre over $\bar x$ is nonempty: choose a point of $Y$ over $x$ using surjectivity, and embed its finite residue extension into the algebraically closed geometric residue field. Thus the diagonal $M\to\prod_{\bar y}M$ is injective. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $(\ker a)_{\bar x}=0$ at every point; [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to $0\to\ker a$, implies $\ker a=0$. All maps are $\Lambda$-linear, so this is also a monomorphism of module sheaves. Define $Q=\operatorname{coker}a$, obtaining $0\to A\to B\to Q\to0$.

The constant sheaves $A$ and $\underline M_Y$ are finite locally constant: their global constant descriptions trivialize them on the single stratum consisting of the entire scheme. They are therefore constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-morphism] to the finite map $\nu$ with finite-type target $X$ to see that $B$ is constructible. Since the coefficient ring in [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions] is finite and commutative, [thm-constructible-serre] applies and shows that $Q=\operatorname{coker}a$ is constructible.

Let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. For an etale $W\to U$, the assumption that $\nu$ is an isomorphism over $U$ identifies $W\times_XY$ with $W$. Hence the unit $a$ restricted to $U$ is an isomorphism, by the section formula for direct image in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] implies $j^{-1}Q=0$; this can be checked on underlying abelian sheaves and hence also on module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $Q$. Its left term $j_!j^{-1}Q$ is zero, so its canonical unit identifies $Q$ with $i_*G$, where $G=i^{-1}Q$. By [prop-constructible-pullback], $G$ is constructible on $Z$.

Apply [lem-fin-closed-immersion] to $i$ and $G$ to obtain $R^bi_*G=0$ for $b>0$. In the spectral sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] for $i$ followed by $f$, only the row $b=0$ remains: every differential to or from that row is zero, and the filtration in total degree $q$ has only one nonzero graded piece, in bidegree $(q,0)$. Indeed the zero graded pieces in positions $p<q$ give $F^0=F^q$, and $F^{q+1}=0$, so $F^q/F^{q+1}=R^qf_*i_*G$ identifies the abutment with this object. This gives $R^qf_*i_*G\cong R^q(fi)_*G$. With $Q\cong i_*G$, apply [lem-fin-finite-morphism] to the assumed finite map $fi:Z\to S$. This proves that $H=f_*Q=(fi)_*G$ is constructible and $R^qf_*Q=0$ for $q>0$. The targets $X,S$ are of finite type as required, and $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $X$.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary short exact sequence of module sheaves on $Y$, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] computes its direct-image stalks as finite products of the original stalks. These products preserve exact sequences by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]; the homology sheaves of the resulting sequence have zero stalks, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to their maps from zero shows they vanish. Thus $
u_*$ is exact, also on module sheaves since kernels and cokernels carry the induced module structures. Choose an injective resolution $\underline M_Y	o I^ ullet$, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Exactness makes $B	o
u_*I^ ullet$ a resolution, and [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] makes every term injective. The computation of derived direct image in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] therefore represents $Rf_*B$ by $f_*
u_*I^ ullet$ and $Rv_*\underline M_Y$ by $v_*I^ ullet$. For every etale $W	o S$, the associativity identification $(W	imes_SX)	imes_XY=W	imes_SY$ identifies these complexes term by term, including differentials. The canonical derived composition comparison is this identification on these injective representatives. Hence it gives natural isomorphisms $R^qf_*B\cong R^qv_*\underline M_Y$ for all $q\geq0$, and composing with $R^qf_*(a)$ is exactly the unit/composition comparison specified in the statement.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and the left-exact additive direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] to apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to $0\to A\to B\to Q\to0$. Substituting the identifications and vanishing proved above gives $0\to f_*A\to v_*\underline M_Y\to H\to R^1f_*A\to R^1v_*\underline M_Y\to0$. In particular $f_*A$ is the kernel of $v_*\underline M_Y\to H$, and with $C=\operatorname{coker}(v_*\underline M_Y\to H)$ there is a short exact sequence $0\to C\to R^1f_*A\to R^1v_*\underline M_Y\to0$. For $q\geq2$, the same long exact sequence has segment $0=R^{q-1}f_*Q\to R^qf_*A\to R^qv_*\underline M_Y\to R^qf_*Q=0$; exactness shows the middle comparison is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs; Stacks 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), parts (1) and (2)

proof.text: By hypothesis $v_*\underline M_Y$ and $R^1v_*\underline M_Y$ are constructible, and $H$ is constructible by step 4. The kernel and cokernel assertion of [thm-constructible-serre] makes $f_*A$ and $C$ constructible. Its extension assertion applied to the short exact sequence in step 6 makes $R^1f_*A$ constructible. For $q\geq2$, step 6 identifies $R^qf_*A$ with the constructible sheaf $R^qv_*\underline M_Y$ from the hypothesis. This proves all constructibility assertions and the specified natural isomorphisms.
